newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down in slow trading on weak sentiment on Thursday but off an intra-day low of 48.959 points due to some bargain hunting, brokers said.
The index fell 0.191 points or 0.39 percent to 49.197 points, on volume of 6.0 million shares worth $2.2 million. Of 41 B shares, 31 traded, with 13 down, 11 flat and seven up.
Brokers said that some bargin hunting made up some of the early losses, but market sentiment was still poor.
"After sharp losses on Wednesday, selling pressure fell a little this afternoon as institutions are waiting for a rebound to sell off their shares," one broker said.
"Rumours that Beijing had held a meeting discussing the B share market also made both selling and buying cautious," a second broker said.
"The index will probably stay around this level before it is officially confirmed," he added.
Eastern Communications was the biggest loser, falling $0.020 or 2.77 percent to $0.700 on volume of 171,000 shares.

Shanghai Automation Instrumentation traded most and was the biggest winner on one institution's speculative buying, soaring $0.020 or 14.28 percent to $0.160 on volume of 1.1 million shares. It had been the biggest loser early in the session.
Shanghai A shares were up on a technical rebound after sharp losses yesterday, and its direction will be dominated by market news in the short term, brokers said.
The A index rose 9.064 points or 1.14 percent to 804.322 points, on volume of 182.4 million shares worth 1.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 gained 25.206 points or 1.24 percent to 2057.149 points.
Sichuan Electric was the star, jumping 0.77 yuan or 12.66 percent to 6.85 yuan on volume of 2.3 million shares.
